marta: Quick sync: we need an apples-to-apples methodology for long-context perf (kernel selection + batching + KV behavior). Can we land on a protocol today?
kevin: +1. high-level: 3 workloads: prefill-heavy (docs -> long generation), steady-chat (mixed seq len), short-burst. Use same seed + replay traces for reproducibility.
sasha: agree. also include a synthetic longmix that matches the seqlen CDF so kernel heuristics see identical distributions.
vikram: perf note: previous run showed ~12% p95 regression on prefill-dominant traces, looks like kernelselect moved to a small-matmul path for long seqs.
marta: can you paste the profiling snippet that points to that?
sasha: sure. profiling top lines: aten::matmul (45%), kv_cache::write (22%), sched_batching::pack (8%). p95 jumped 320ms -> 358ms on A100-80G.
sasha: command we used: 
```bash
./replay_harness --trace traces/longprefill_1k.json --model rwd-open-7b --kernelselect=auto --batcher=continuous --workers=16 --seed=42
```
kevin: To be apples-to-apples we should force kernelselect=legacy and also a quant-mode run. And compare cold vs warm KV cache.
marta: Agreed. experiment matrix: (kernelselect: auto/legacy/force-quant) x (cache: cold/warm) x (3 seeds). Collect p50/p95/tokens_s/kernel_choice_counts.
vikram: Also capture batch_pack_size and seqlen_hist per minute. Add KV hit rate and kv_write_latency.
perf-bot: Scheduled jobs created: job/1898765432-longctx-compare-1..18
sasha: Quick snapshot from a warm vs cold auto run: warm p95=340ms, cold p95=560ms. KV hit rate warm=87% cold=12%.
marta: That suggests prefill write path dominates cold-case. Potential mitigations: eager prefix caching, or prioritize a prefill-specific kernel to avoid the matmul tiling switch.
kevin: I suggest adding a prefill-only kernel path that keeps larger matmul tiles for long continuous prefill and bypasses the tiling heuristics.
sasha: I'll add a microbenchmark: single-request prefill 1k tokens with KV-only writes to isolate the write path perf.
marta: timeline? would like initial runs in next 24h so we can present in eng-runtime sync.
vikram: I can kick cluster runs overnight and post the job links + artifacts here (perf dashboards, flamegraphs).
marta: thx. also please ensure apples-to-apples doc includes exact docker image, driver and env (CUDA/cuDNN/pytorch) versions.
kevin: env we'll standardize on: CUDA=12.1, cuDNN=8.5, pytorch=2.2, rwd-runtime=1.9.2, kernel-build-id in metadata.
sasha: noted — will tag outputs with git sha and kernel_build_id and include flamegraph + perf counters.
marta: cool. closing for now — ping the thread when the first results land :thumbsup:
